To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maximum dry matter losses were in the wettest and warmest treatments, and the maximum ZEN production was in the warmest and wettest treatments.
(a) CO2 production rates were increased by F. gramineanum and were affected by aw and temperature; (b) CO2 production was related to DMLs and (c) ZEA contamination was related to DMI losses.
the maximum dry matter losses were in the 20 25 deg C and 0.95 water activity treatments and that at ca. 1% DML, risk of exceeding the EU legislative limits for ZEN was low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a decision support system to aid post harvest decisions on the relative risk of ZEN and other Fusarium mycotoxines in wheat.
the development of indicators of relative risk of exceeding EU legislative limits for mycotoxin contamination in wheat.
the effect of environmental conditions on the growth of Fusarium graminearium in wheat, and its impact on ZEN contamination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative risk of ZEN exceeding the EU limits was low at DMLs < 1%, and high at > 1.0%.
the risk of ZEN exceeding legislative limits is related to the DMLs and that this can be quantified using respiration rates and CO2 production.
the relative risks of ZEN contamination in stored wheat are dependent on environmental conditions, with a higher relative risk in wetter and/or warmer conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the respiration rate and DMLs are good indicators of the risk of mycotoxin contamination, and can be used as an early warning system to prevent the contamination of wheat grain.
CO2 production can be used as a reliable indicator of DMLs in stored wheat and this can be used to estimate the relative risk of ZEN exceeding legislative limits.

respiration rate is a reliable indicator of DMLs and ZEN production in wheat, which can be used to develop a post harvest decision making system to manage relative risks of mycotoxin contamination in wheat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative risk of exceeding the EU legislative limits for ZEN contamination can be predicted by measuring dry matter losses.

the respiration rate of wheat grain, as measured by the CO2 production, could be used as a proxy for the relative risks of different levels of dry matter loss, and thus the relative risks of exceeding the EU legislative limits for ZEN contamination in wheat grain.
respiration rate and DML can be used to estimate the relative risk of exceeding the EU legislative limits of ZEN contamination in stored grain.
